The future of mobile CPUs, part 1: Today’s fork in the road | Ars Technica
2013 may be a big year for the evolution of smartphones and tablets.
Mobile computing's rise from niche market to the mainstream is among the most significant technological trends in our lifetimes. Initially, most mobile devices relied on highly specialized hardware to meet stringent power and size budgets. But with so many transors available, devices inevitably grew general-purpose capabilities. The initial desire was probably to reduce costs by creating a more flexible software ecosystem with better re-use and faster time to market. As such, the first smartphones were very much a novelty, and it took many years before the world realized the potential of such devices. Apple played a major role by creating innovative smartphones that consumers craved and quickly adopted.
To some extent, this is where we still stand today. Smartphones are still (relatively) expensive and primarily interesting to the developed world. But over the next 10 years, this too will change. As Moore’s Law rolls on, the cost of a low-end smartphone will decline. At some point, the incremental cost will be quite minimal and many feature phones of today will be supplanted by smartphones. In this grand progression, 2013 will certainly be a significant milestone for mobile devices, smartphones and beyond. And in the coming years, this will lead to a confluence of high-end tablets and ultra-mobile notebooks as the world figures out how these devices co-exist, blend, hybridize, and/or merge.
Against this backdrop, in this two-part series, we'll explore the major trends and evolution for mobile SoCs. More importantly, we'll look to where the major vendors are likely going in the next several years.
Tablet and phone divergence
While phones and tablets are mobile devices that often share a great deal of software, it's becoming increasingly clear the two are very different products. From a technical perspective, smartphones are far more compact and power constrained. For the cost sensitive-models that make up the vast majority of the market, the modem is integrated into the SoC itself. High-end designs favor discreteems with a greater power budget instead. The main smartphone OSes today are iOS and Android, though Windows is beginning to make an appearance (perhaps with Linux or BlackBerry on the horizon). Just as importantly, phone vendors like HTC must pass government certification and win the approval of carriers. There is very much a walled-garden aspect, where carriers control which devices can be attached to their networks, and in some cases devices can only be sold through a certain carrier. The business model places consumers quite far removed from the actual hardware.
In contrast, tablets are far more akin to the PC both technically and economically. The power budget for tablet SoCs is much greater, up to 4W for a passively cooled device and as high as 7-8W for systems with fans. This alone means there is a much wider range of tablet designs than smartphones. The vast majority of tablets do not have cellularems, and even fewer customers actually purchase a wireless data plan. As a result, cellularems are almost always optional discrete components of the platform. The software ecosystem is relatively similar, with Microsoft, Apple, and Google OSes available. Because tablets eschew cellularems, the time to market is faster, and they are much more commonly sold directly to consumers rather than through carriers. In terms of usage models, tablets are much more PC-like, with reasonable-sized screens that make games and media more attractive.
Looking forward, these distinctions will likely become more pronounced. As the markets grow in volume, SoCs will inevitably bifurcate to focus on one market or the other. Even today, Apple is doing so, with the A6 for phones and the larger A6X for tablets. Other vendors may need to wait a few years to have the requisite volume, but eventually the two markets will be clearly separate.
Horizontal business model evolution
Another aspect of the mobile device market that is currently in flux and likely to change in the coming years is the business model for the chip and system vendors. Currently, Apple is the only company truly pursuing a vertically integrated model, where all phones and tablets are based on Apple’s own SoC designs and iOS. The tight integration between hardware and software has been a huge boon for Apple, and it has yielded superb products.
Samsung is one of the few others companies that takes a vertically integrated approach to phones and tablets, although in truth its strategy seems to be ambivalent on that point. Unlike Apple, Samsung’s SoCs are readily available to third parties, and some Samsung devices, such as the S7562 Galaxy S Duos, use SoCs from competitors. More recently though, there has been a trend of Samsung devices using Samsung SoCs, at least for the premier products. For the moment, Samsung’s approach is best characterized as a hybrid, particularly as the company lacks a bespoke OS.
The rest of the major SoC vendors (e.g., Intel, Qualcomm, Nvidia, TI, Mediatek, etc.) have stayed pretty far away from actual mobile devices. These companies tend to focus on horizontal business models that avoid competing with customers or suppliers.
In the long term, mobile devices are likely to evolve similarly to the PC and favor a horizontal business model. The real advantage is one of flexibility; as costs drop and the market expands, it will be increasingly necessary for vendors like HTC to offer a wide range of phones based on radically different SoCs. While a vertically integrated company like Apple can focus and maintain leadership in a specific (and highly lucrative) niche, it would be very difficult to expand in many growing areas of the market. However, SoC vendors will attempt to reap the benefits of vertical integration by providing complete reference platforms to OEMs. Conceptually, this is a form of "optional" system integration, where the phone vendor or carrier can get the entire platform from the SoC supplier. This has the principal advantages of reducing time to market while also providing a baseline quality and experience for consumers. Currently, this approach has mostly been tested in emerging markets, but it's likely to become more common over time. There is a crucial distinction between reference platforms and vertical integration. Namely, OEMs can always choose to customize a platform to differentiate, and the SoC vendor avoids dealing with consumers directly. Off topic: show

I'm not so sure about several things:1- Moore's law's relevance. ICs are not as big a part of mobile computers as they are of desktops, even of laptops: screens, batteries, radios are a huge part of tablets' and phones' costs, as opposed to the bare SoC + RAM.2- The tablet vs phone dichotomy. Since the OS and peripherals are the same, it makes more sense to design and build just one type of SoC, and just disable the phone-modem part of it (even the other radios are still required: BT, Wifi, GPS...), same as Intel disable cache and cores for their entry-level CPUs. Once you're fabbing a SoC, it makes more sense to make more of the same than to setup a separate run of a cut-down SoC on an older process, unless volumes are huge. results.question: What is the main advantage of a horizontal business model for mobile devices?
answers: Flexibility.
results.compressed_docs:
Mobile computing's rise from niche market to the mainstream is among the most significant technological trends in our lifetimes. Initially, most mobile devices relied on highly specialized hardware to meet stringent power and size budgets. Apple played a major role by creating innovative smartphones that consumers craved and quickly adopted.
From a technical perspective, smartphones are far more compact and power constrained. There is very much a walled-garden aspect, where carriers control which devices can be attached to their networks, and in some cases devices can only be sold through a certain carrier. The business model places consumers quite far removed from the actual hardware.
This alone means there is a much wider range of tablet designs than smartphones. The vast majority of tablets do not have cellularems, and even fewer customers actually purchase a wireless data plan. As a result, cellular modems are almost always optional discrete components of the platform. The software ecosystem is relatively similar, with Microsoft, Apple, and Google OSes available. Because tablets eschew cellularems, the time to market is faster, and they are much more commonly sold directly to consumers rather than through carriers. Other vendors may need to wait a few years to have the requisite volume, but eventually the two markets will be clearly separate.
Horizontal business model evolution
Another aspect of the mobile device market that is currently in flux and likely to change in the coming years is the business model for the chip and system vendors. Currently, Apple is the only company truly pursuing a vertically integrated model, where all phones and tablets are based on Apple’s own SoC designs and iOS. Samsung is one of the few others companies that takes a vertically integrated approach to phones and tablets, although in truth its strategy seems to be ambivalent on that point. Unlike Apple, Samsung’s SoCs are readily available to third parties, and some Samsung devices, such as the S7562 Galaxy S Duos, use SoCs from competitors. The rest of the major SoC vendors (e.g., Intel, Qualcomm, Nvidia, TI, Mediatek, etc.) have stayed pretty far away from actual mobile devices. These companies tend to focus on horizontal business models that avoid competing with customers or suppliers.
In the long term, mobile devices are likely to evolve similarly to the PC and favor a horizontal business model. The real advantage is one of flexibility; as costs drop and the market expands, it will be increasingly necessary for vendors like HTC to offer a wide range of phones based on radically different SoCs. While a vertically integrated company like Apple can focus and maintain leadership in a specific (and highly lucrative) niche, it would be very difficult to expand in many growing areas of the market. However, SoC vendors will attempt to reap the benefits of vertical integration by providing complete reference platforms to OEMs. Conceptually, this is a form of "optional" system integration, where the phone vendor or carrier can get the entire platform from the SoC supplier. This has the principal advantages of reducing time to market while also providing a baseline quality and experience for consumers. Currently, this approach has mostly been tested in emerging markets, but it's likely to become more common over time. There is a crucial distinction between reference platforms and vertical integration. Namely, OEMs can always choose to customize a platform to differentiate, and the SoC vendor avoids dealing with consumers directly. Off topic: show

Political Theory and American Politics
Professoris's interests bridge the of political theory and American politics, including more specifically, American political development, constitutional theory, political philosophy and the American presidency. His publications include The Presidency in the Constitutional Order (LSU 981; Transaction 010), The Rhetorical Presidency (inceton 987), The Constitutional Presidency (John Hopkins 009), The Limits of Constitutional Democracy (inceton010) and recent journal articles and chapters on constitutional interpretation, the of political change, and the meaning of political success. Four collections of essays on Thehet Presidency with responses byis have been published, including a special double issue of Critical Review: Andisciplinary Journal of Politics and Society, (007), where his book is described as " of the two or three most important andceptive works written by a political scientist in the century."
He has served as President of the Politics and History Section the American Association. He received the President's Associates Teaching Excellence Award at the of Texas. He has held research fellowships fromH, ACLS, Olin Foundation, Harvard Law School, and the Mellon Preceptorship at Princeton University, where he taught before moving to Texas. He has held visiting positions at Dame and Harvard. He has served as associate chair of the Department of Government from 989-001 and was acting chair during 992-93. and for part of each year between 1989 and 001. During the academic year 008-09, he was a Laurance S. Rockefelleriting Fellow at the University Center for Human Values at Princeton. During Spring 016, he was a Dahorfiting Fellow at the Economics and Science.
His forthcoming books include: Legacies of Losing in American Politics, with Nicole Mellow (University of Chicago Press, Fall 017), and an expanded of The Presidency in the Princeton Classics series (inceton,17). For two decades he served as co-editor of the Hopkins Series in Constitutional Thought, and he currently coits (with Sanford Levinson) Constitutional Thinking, a Series at the University Press of Kansas.

On,P airs local sports shows from 9 a .m. and carries ESPN programming weekday mornings, late nights and weekends. SomeP shows are on other sports stations in the region.

It shares clear-channel, Class A status on AM with WFED.C. P broadcasts a directional signal at night, using a threeower array, with its transmitter on U. 61 at Beam Avenue in Maplewood.  History

WAMD and KFOY
KP's start in928 was the of a merger between two pioneering Cities stations:AMD ("Where All Minneapolis D") in Minneapolis, first licensed on 125 to Stanley. HubbardY in on 12 to the Beacon Radio Service in Paul.

Following a few test transmissions,AMD its formal debut on 225. (In later interviews Hubbard traced's start to124.) It was located at the Marold Dance Garden, and featured nightly "night Fros" broadcasts by theroom's orchestra. Beginning on 21927 theAMD broadcasts, still on 1330 , were toY's facility in Paul. National Battery Company
In mid-December27, the Company announced it had received permission the Federal Commission to build a new station, with the letters KP, operating from a transmitter site to be constructed three miles of Wott.P its debut on 28. Hubbard became the merged's manager, acquiring in941. A month after the,P became an affiliate for the NBC Red Network.  It remained with NBC for 4 years. On 192, under the theRC's General Order 4,P was assigned to a "high-powered regional" frequency1460 kHz. results.question: How are smartphones and tablets different from a technical perspective?
answers: Smartphones are more compact and power constrained.

The future of mobile CPUs, part 1: Today’s fork in the road | Ars Technica
2013 may be a big year for the evolution of smartphones and tablets.
Mobile computing's rise from niche market to the mainstream is among the most significant technological trends in our lifetimes. And to a large extent, it's been driven by the bounty of Moore’s Law—the rule that transistor density doubles every 24 months. Initially, most mobile devices relied on highly specialized hardware to meet stringent power and size budgets. As such, the first smartphones were very much a novelty, and it took many years before the world realized the potential of such devices. Apple played a major role by creating innovative smartphones that consumers craved and quickly adopted.
Smartphones are still (relatively) expensive and primarily interesting to the developed world. A $650 unsubsidized phone is well beyond the reach of most of the world compared to a $20 feature phone, but a $30 to $40 smartphone would naturally be very popular.
In this grand progression, 2013 will certainly be a significant milestone for mobile devices, smartphones and beyond. It's likely to be the first year in which tablets out-ship notebooks in the US. And in the coming years, this will lead to a confluence of high-end tablets and ultra-mobile notebooks as the world figures out how these devices co-exist, blend, hybridize, and/or merge.
Against this backdrop, in this two-part series, we'll explore the major trends and evolution for mobile SoCs. Tablet and phone divergence
While phones and tablets are mobile devices that often share a great deal of software, it's becoming increasingly clear the two are very different products. These two markets have started to diverge and will continue doing so over time.
From a technical perspective, smartphones are far more compact and power constrained. For the cost sensitive-models that make up the vast majority of the market, the modem is integrated into the SoC itself. High-end designs favor discreteems with a greater power budget instead. The main smartphone OSes today are iOS and Android, though Windows is beginning to make an appearance (perhaps with Linux or BlackBerry on the horizon). There is very much a walled-garden aspect, where carriers control which devices can be attached to their networks, and in some cases devices can only be sold through a certain carrier. In contrast, tablets are far more akin to the PC both technically and economically. The power budget for tablet SoCs is much greater, up to 4W for a passively cooled device and as high as 7-8W for systems with fans. This alone means there is a much wider range of tablet designs than smartphones. Moreover, the default connectivity for tablets is Wi-Fi rather than a cellular modem. The vast majority of tablets do not have cellularems, and even fewer customers actually purchase a wireless data plan. As a result, cellularems are almost always optional discrete components of the platform. The software ecosystem is relatively similar, with Microsoft, Apple, and Google OSes available. Because tablets eschew cellularems, the time to market is faster, and they are much more commonly sold directly to consumers rather than through carriers. In terms of usage models, tablets are much more PC-like, with reasonable-sized screens that make games and media more attractive.
Looking forward, these distinctions will likely become more pronounced. Many tablets today use high-end smartphone SoCs, but the difference in power targets and expected performance is quite large. As the markets grow in volume, SoCs will inevitably bifurcate to focus on one market or the other. Even today, Apple is doing so, with the A6 for phones and the larger A6X for tablets. Other vendors may need to wait a few years to have the requisite volume, but eventually the two markets will be clearly separate.
Horizontal business model evolution
Another aspect of the mobile device market that is currently in flux and likely to change in the coming years is the business model for the chip and system vendors. Currently, Apple is the only company truly pursuing a vertically integrated model, where all phones and tablets are based on Apple’s own SoC designs and iOS. The tight integration between hardware and software has been a huge boon for Apple, and it has yielded superb products.
Samsung is one of the few others companies that takes a vertically integrated approach to phones and tablets, although in truth its strategy seems to be ambivalent on that point. Unlike Apple, Samsung’s SoCs are readily available to third parties, and some Samsung devices, such as the S7562 Galaxy S Duos, use SoCs from competitors. More recently though, there has been a trend of Samsung devices using Samsung SoCs, at least for the premier products. have stayed pretty far away from actual mobile devices. In the long term, mobile devices are likely to evolve similarly to the PC and favor a horizontal business model. The real advantage is one of flexibility; as costs drop and the market expands, it will be increasingly necessary for vendors like HTC to offer a wide range of phones based on radically different SoCs. While a vertically integrated company like Apple can focus and maintain leadership in a specific (and highly lucrative) niche, it would be very difficult to expand in many growing areas of the market. However, SoC vendors will attempt to reap the benefits of vertical integration by providing complete reference platforms to OEMs. Conceptually, this is a form of "optional" system integration, where the phone vendor or carrier can get the entire platform from the SoC supplier. Namely, OEMs can always choose to customize a platform to differentiate, and the SoC vendor avoids dealing with consumers directly. Typically, most of the customization is in terms of software on top of a base operating system.

The specification relates to a system and method for generating a of content for a channel. In particular, the specification to generating a of content for a channel based on user interests and historical trends.
Many consumers of digital media have two somewhat contradictory goals: keep appised of information in the areas they already find interesting and discover new content that is also enjoyable. Hence, there is a need to present the best and most relevant information, without overwhelming the consumer. As a result, there is also a need to cater to the time dependent changes in the consumer's interests while presenting information., discovering new content is difficult when the consumer is overed with existing content.
Prior attempts to solve these problems allow consumers to create personalized sections in feed aggregation websites that are defined by keywords. Often, these personalized sections present any item that includes the keywords even though the item is not of interest to the consumer, per se. In another method, consumers are allowed to manually subscribe to ReallyicationRSS) feeds from multiple websites. In some examples, the specification describes a system and method for generating a of content for a channel using a channel application. answers: Symptoms of vitamin K deficiency include anemia, bruising, nosebleeds, bleeding of the gums, and heavy menstrual bleeding in women.

results.question: What happens to the high resolution of what we focus on at dawn or dusk?
answers: It becomes a bit less so that what's off to the left or right can be better noted.
results.compressed_docs:
Our inner viewport is ever only that of the model (qualia) of inner and outer reality built by the brain. We see/sense nothing but this model made inside the brain.
We don't see across a room or any scene but only across the model of the roomscene. We't look through a microscope at an actual object but only look at a model of that object. You get the idea. A reflective color spectrum is used to make it look like that more distinctive color is a surface property of an object modeled.
The brain't model everything, as a lot of it would be clutter, and for what remains as useful to portray the brain still't have the resources to model everything at high resolution and so thus whatever we on gets all the high res detail put into it just in the time when we lookocus. At dawn dusk this high resolution becomes a bit less on what we focus on so that what's off to the left or right can be better noted in the dim light.
So far, nothing astounding here to us, although maybe to everyday folk that we only ever see the inside of the head/brain—the model.
Of course, the shocks get worse, such as that our intentions cannot be those of first cause, self-made people, but from prior causes that we't to choose and be responsible for. What is left, in short, is the freedom of action for these inbuilt intentions to operate, at least when not prevented by the weather or any other controlling factors, which 'edom of action' amounts to compatibilism.

, researchers \{020ariv00511552C,01991103029L} first have to divide the training data into two subsets, including a new subset of data and a new of data, and then train their proposed method and other \{SOTA} methods. results.question: Which orders did Mufti-e-Azam-e-Hind receive Khilafat from?
answers: Mufti-e-Azam-e-Hind received Khilafat in the Qaderi, Chishti, Nakshbandi, Suharwardi, and Madaari Orders.

Ghousul Waqt,i-eam-eind (radiahu anhu) was born on Monday, 22nd of Zil Hijjah 1310 AH (18 July1892) in the most beautiful city of Bareilly Shareef, India. At the time of the birth ofousul Waqt,i-eam-eind (radihu), his distinguished father, was in Mahrerah Shareef, one of the great spiritual centers of the Sunni World.i-eamind (hu) was later named "Musta Raza Khan". Upon the birth of Waqt,i-eamindhu) Sayyiduna Shah Abul Hussain Ahmadi Noori (radihu) told A'la Hazrat (radiahu anhu), "Maulana! As promised, when Sayyiduna Abul Hussain Ahadiori (radihu) went to Bareillyef, he immediately summoned to seefti-eam-eind (radiahuhu) who was only six (6) months old.una Noori Mia (radihu), as he was also famously known, congratulated A'laratradihu) and said, "This child will be of great assistance to the Deen and through him the servants of Almighty Allah will gain great benefit. This child is a Wali. From his blessed sight thousands of stray Muslims will become firm on theen. On saying this,unaori Miaradihu) placed his blessed finger into the mouth of-eam-eind (radi Allahu anhu) and made him a Mureed. He also blessed him with I'jaazat and Khilafat at the same time. (Mufti Azam Hind Number, pg. Not only did he receiveat in the Qaderi Silsila (Order), but also in the Chishti, Nakshbandi, Suharwardi, and Madaari Orders.i-e-Azam-eind (radiahu anhu) also receivedat from his blessed father, A'larat, Ash Shah Imam Ahmed Raza Khan Al Qaderi (radihu).
Gousul Waqt,i-eam-eind (radihu) attained most of his early education from hisrious family - from his father, A'larat, Ash Shah Imam Ahmedaza Khan Al Qi (radi Allahu anhu) the Mujaddid of Islam, whose status and position even at that time cannot be explained in these few lines. He also studied Kitaabs under the guidance of Hazrat Moulana Haamid Raza Khan (his elder brother), Maulana Shah Rahm Ilahi Maglori and Maulana Sayed Basheer Ahmad Aligarhi and Maulana Zahurul Hussain Rampuri (radi Allahu anhum). He studied various branches of knowledge under the guidance of his most learned and blessed father, A'larat (radi anhu). He gained proficiency in the many branches of Islamic knowledge from among which are: Tafseer; Hadith; Fiqh; Laws of Jurisudence; Sarf; Nahw; Tajweed; Conduct of Language; Philosophy; Logistics; Mathematics; History etc.; Arithmetic; Aqaid (Belief); Taasawwaf; Poetry; Debating; Sciences; etc.
Mui-eam-eind, Moulana Mustapha Raza Khan (radiahu anhu's) brilliance as an Islamic Scholar manifested itself when he was a still a youth, but overflowing with knowledge and wisdom. He wrote his first historical Fatawa (Islamic Ruling) when was only 13 years old. Hazrat Maulana Zafrud'deen andratana Sayed Abdur Rasheed (radiahu anhum) were at the Darul Ifta (Fatawa Department) at this stage. One day,i-ezam-eind (radi anhu) walked into theula and noticed thatratana Zafrudeen (radi anhu) was writing a certainwa. He was taking "Fatawa Razvia" from the shelf as his reference. On seeing this,i-e-Azam-eind (radi anhu) said, "Are you relying onatawa Razvia to write an answer?" Mufti-e-Azam-eind (radi anhu) then wrote a powerful answer without any problem. This was the Fwa concerning "Raza'at" - the very firstwa which he had written.
Sayyiduna A'larat (radi anhu) then signed thewa. He also commanded Hafiz Yaqeenudeen (radi anhu) to make a stamp fori-eam-eindradihu) as a gift and said that it should read as follows: "Abul Barkaat Muhiy'yuddeen Jilani Aale Rahmaan urf Mustapha Raza Khan."
After this incidenti-e-eind, Mana Mustaaza Khan (radi anhu) spent another 12 years writing Fatawas at the feet of Alarat (radi anhu). He was given this immense responsibility of issuingatawas even whilelarat (radihu) was in this physical world. Mui-e-eind (radi anhu) married the blessed daughter of his paternal uncle,rat Muhammad Raza Khan (radi anhu). "Khuda Kheyr se Laaye Wo Din Bhi Noori, Madine ki Galiya Buhara Karoo me"
Tajedaare Ahle Sunnah, Taaje Wilayat Wa Karaamat, Mufti-eam-eind, Mana Mustaaza Khan (radi anhu) went twice for Hajj - in1905 and945. Mui-e-Aam-eind, Mana Mustaaza Khan (radi anhu) was the first person to go for Hajj without a photograph in his passport.-e-A-eind (radihu) was allowed to go forj without a photograph in his passport and without taking any vaccinations.
During his trip to Makkatul Mukarramah,-e-eindradihu), also had the opportunity of meeting those Uma whom his father, Sayidduna A'laratradi anhu), met during his visit to Haramain Sharifain. These greatma were from amongst the students of Sayedya Almaan (radi anhu). A few of the Uma that he met were Allamah Sayed Ameen Qutbi; Allah Sayed Abbas Alawi and Allah Sayed Noor Muhammad (radiahu anhum) - to mention just few. They narrated many incidents which had place during Sayyiduna A'laratradi anhu's) visit toain Sharifain. They then requested Khilafat from Mui-e-A-eind, (radi anhu) which he bestowed upon them.
Tajarelenah, Taatamat,-e-A-eind, Mana Mustaaza Khanradi anhu) was aware of the actual time of his Wisaal.
On the 6th of Muharram (1981) he said, "All those who intended to become my Mureed but for some reason or other not come to me, I have made all of themureed and I have given their hands into the hand of Sayidduna Ghousul Azam (radi anhu)."
On the 1th of Mam, he again asked concerning the date and the Mureedeen present said that it was Wednesday, the 1th ofam. Mu-e-Aam-eind (radi anhu) was not only giving hope to the Mureedeen but also informing them of his Wal.
The shining star of A'larat, Ash Shah Imam Ahmedaza Khan (radi anhu), the glitter and the hope for the hearts of millions throughout the world, the Mujaddid of the 15th Century, the Imam of his time, Huzoor Sayyidi Sarkaar Mui-e-am-eind (radi anhu) left the Aalame Duniya to Journey towards the Aame Aakhira.
